facts.statement: The genus Dicksonosteus was described by Goujet in 1975.
Dicksonosteus lived during the Early Devonian period in Spitsbergen, Norway.
facts.quote: Dicksonosteus is an extinct genus of basal arthrodire placoderm fish which lived during the Early Devonian period of Spitsbergen, Norway.

facts.statement: Dicksonosteus was once classified as an actinolepid but is now placed in the family Phlyctaeniidae.
facts.quote: Dicksonosteus was once considered an actinolepid, but is now grouped within the family Phlyctaeniidae.

facts.statement: Dicksonosteus is most closely related to the genera Arctolepis and Heintzosteus.
facts.quote: Dicksonosteus is most closely related to Arctolepis and Heintzosteus.

facts.statement: Dicksonosteus had a wide, flat body and relatively feeble jaws compared to later arthrodires like Dunkleosteus.
facts.quote: Its body is wide and flat, and unlike the more robust-jawed arthrodires that would come after it, such as Dunkleosteus and Coccosteus, its jaws were relatively feeble

facts.statement: Its feeble jaws suggest Dicksonosteus was a benthic fish that ate smaller, softer-bodied animals.
facts.quote: suggesting the lifestyle of a benthic fish that subsisted primarily on smaller, softer-bodied animals.

facts.statement: Exceptionally preserved fossils from Spitsbergen show details of Dicksonosteus's braincase and internal anatomy.
facts.quote: Exceptionally preserved fossil specimens of Dicksonosteus from Spitsbergen, Norway display details of its braincase and internal anatomy

facts.statement: Dicksonosteus lived from the Pragian to the Emsian stages, between 413.02 and 393.47 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Pragian to Emsian (413.02 to 393.47 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dicksonosteus belongs to the class Placodermi.
